title: Recursion
summary: A base case, a smaller subproblem, and an honest stack story.

parts.rule: State a base case, a smaller subproblem, and what the stack holds between calls. If you cannot name those three, the recursive story is not ready.

body:
Rule. State a base case, a smaller subproblem, and what the stack holds between calls. If you cannot name those three, the recursive story is not ready.

Why it matters. Trees, partitions, and divide-and-conquer read cleanly as recursion. Interviews still want the stack picture so you can convert to an explicit stack or spot a depth blow-up before it crashes.

SAMPLE example. SAMPLE: factorial of n multiplies n by factorial of n-1 until n is 0. The base case returns 1. Each frame waits for a smaller n. Depth is n, so space is linear unless the language can optimize the tail.

When to use. Use recursion when the input decomposes into similar smaller inputs and the merge step is obvious. Prefer it for tree walks and for backtracking outlines before you optimize.

When to refuse. Refuse recursion on a linked chain of length n if a simple loop suffices and depth would mirror n. Refuse missing base cases. Refuse claiming constant space while the call stack still grows with the input.
